title: Returning from ACPI sleep causes an unhandled loss of vulkan context
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible version: Godot Engine v4.4.beta.custom_build.a013481b0 (2025-01-28 22:08:59 UTC)
	Vulkan 1.3.242 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB
	(using Debian Linux)
- Previous version used to hang up instead, thus the lack of a report (no error was output).

### System information

Godot v4.4.beta (a013481b0) - Debian GNU/Linux trixie/sid trixie on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB (nvidia) - AMD Ryzen 5 1600 Six-Core Processor (12 threads)

(I could build with debug symbols if necessary)

The fault happens when the computer goes to sleep mode while the editor is open. This kills the editor without recourse.
Would it be possible to add a check for this exception and either recreate the context from scratch, or at least gracefully save a backup and quit?
It is not a huge deal, as it is rare that you'd leave the editor running without saving changes, but it can happen and cause data loss. Either way, the crash could be handled better as nothing informs the user that godot even closed unless stdout is visible.

Thank you.


### Steps to reproduce

- Open the editor.
- Activate ACPI sleep or hibernation.
- Return from it.
- Crash.
